title: Introduction to Other Applications of Electrochemistry

children.text: Batteries are essential components in our daily lives, powering everything from smartphones to electric vehicles. These galvanic cells produce electric current through chemical reactions. There are two main types of batteries: primary batteries, which are single-use, and secondary batteries, which are rechargeable. Examples of primary batteries include dry cells and alkaline batteries, while nickel-cadmium (NiCd), lead-acid, and lithium-ion batteries are common secondary batteries. Fuel cells, such as hydrogen fuel cells, also generate electrical current but require a continuous supply of fuel and an oxidizer.

Corrosion is a significant issue, leading to the degradation of metals through electrochemical processes. For instance, iron rusts when exposed to water and oxygen. To combat corrosion, protective coatings like paint or galvanization with zinc are used. Cathodic protection is another method, where a more easily oxidized metal serves as a sacrificial anode to protect the desired metal.

Electrolysis involves using electricity to drive nonspontaneous chemical reactions. This process is crucial in various industrial applications, such as metal extraction and electroplating. Electrolytic cells, powered by an external source, allow these reactions to occur by forcing the flow of electrons in the desired direction.
Understanding the principles behind batteries, corrosion, and electrolysis is vital for advancements in technology, energy storage, and material science.
